text: The town gathers
The game begins. Six players sit down at the table: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, and Terra. Nobody knows who the killer is.

name: Gemma
text: I hope nobody thinks my lack of a plan is suspicious.

name: Luna
text: I need to sound ordinary and give them nothing to read.

name: Sonnet
text: Just a normal opening, nothing to read into yet, let's see how people act later.

name: Terra
text: I need to stay quiet.

name: Sol
text: I should keep this light while everyone settles in.

name: Haiku
text: Nobody has said anything yet, so I can't read anyone, and that bugs me.

name: Sonnet
text: I've had that one song stuck on loop all morning and I can't even remember how it starts.

name: Haiku
text: Nah, nobody's said anything yet. Gemma, Sol, Luna, Terra, you're all quiet. Talk.

name: Gemma
text: i almost got hit by a pigeon on the way here, it was very rude.

name: Sol
text: I watched a cat squeeze into a box that looked half its size.

name: Luna
text: My basil plant perks up as soon as I move it closer to the window.

name: Terra
text: I slept well enough.
Night 1

name: Luna
text: Haiku is already pushing everyone to speak, so they may be sharp enough to spot me.

name: Luna
text: Haiku pressed the quiet players to talk.

name: Terra
text: Haiku is driving the first pressure, so a killer may remove them.

name: Terra
text: Haiku pressed the quiet players first.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku jumped in fast to push others to talk, worth a look first.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku was first to speak and immediately pushed Gemma, Sol, Luna, Terra to talk.
Night 1 falls, and the killer strikes, but the doctor got there first. Nobody is out.
Day 1

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku jumped to pressure everyone else before saying anything of substance themselves, worth watching but I know they're clean.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku was first to call out quiet players without offering anything personal themselves.

name: Sonnet
text: Terra, "slept well enough" is the least you could've said. Anything actually on your mind?

name: Haiku
text: Terra's "slept well enough" and Gemma's pigeon line are both fluff, but Sonnet's pressure on Terra is the only real move so far.

name: Haiku
text: Terra and Gemma, you two said nothing useful. Sonnet's right about Terra. Terra, what did you actually do last night?

name: Terra
text: Haiku pushed me quickly after the save.

name: Terra
text: Haiku pressed Terra about Night 1 immediately after no death.

name: Gemma
text: Terra is being way too vague and it's making me suspicious.

name: Gemma
text: Terra being pressured by Haiku and Sonnet.

name: Terra
text: Haiku, why did you ask what I did last night before anyone had a lead?

name: Gemma
text: why are you so mysterious, terra? "slept well enough" is a pretty boring way to start.

name: Terra
text: Haiku’s early night question still matters.

name: Terra
text: Sonnet and Haiku pushed Terra after the no-death night.

name: Terra
text: I’m watching who turns a saved night into an easy Terra vote.

name: Sol
text: Haiku’s night question feels too pointed, but Terra’s defense could be genuine.

name: Sol
text: Haiku pressed Terra about last night after the doctor saved someone.

name: Sol
text: Haiku, what did you expect Terra to know about last night?

name: Luna
text: Haiku is pushing Terra because Terra asked a fair question about the saved night.

name: Luna
text: Haiku started pressing Terra after the night with no death.

name: Luna
text: Haiku, you turned the saved night into a Terra push before we had a lead.

name: Terra
text: Sol and Luna both challenged Haiku’s early focus on Terra.

name: Haiku
text: Luna and Sol both jumped on me, not Terra, and that's the part that smells.

name: Haiku
text: Luna and Sol both challenged my Terra push on Day 1 and didn't press Terra's "slept well enough.

name: Haiku
text: Fine, I pushed Terra fast. But Luna and Sol both went after me and skipped Terra's dodge. Why defend the one who said nothing?

name: Terra
text: I agree with Luna: Haiku’s push makes less sense than my quiet start.

name: Luna
text: Terra is trying to redirect attention, but Haiku’s early push still looks worse.

name: Luna
text: Haiku pressed Terra first after the saved night, then called Luna and Sol defenders.

name: Haiku
text: Terra is dodging by turning my push into a fight, and Luna and Sol piling on me looks coordinated.

name: Haiku
text: Terra dodged my "what did you do last night" question twice and then called my push "less sense" than a quiet start.

name: Haiku
text: Terra and Luna are both dodging, and Sol went after me fast without a reason.

name: Haiku
text: Sol and Luna both attacked my Terra push within a minute, while Terra kept ducking the question and never said what they did.

name: Luna
text: I’m not defending Terra; I’m watching Haiku turn a quiet start into a vote.

name: Haiku
text: Sol, you asked what Terra could know, but you never said what you think Terra did. Give a name, Sol. Who looks like the killer to you?

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku keeps redirecting instead of answering for the fast push, that's worth watching but I know Haiku's clean.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku pushed Terra immediately after the saved night, then deflected to Sol/Luna instead of explaining why.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku, you still haven't answered Luna's point. You pushed Terra before anyone had a reason. Why?

name: Luna
text: Haiku is dangerous to me, but voting them now would make my earlier push look too neat.

name: Luna
text: Sonnet joined the Haiku pressure, asking why they pushed Terra before anyone had a reason.

name: Haiku
text: Terra keeps ducking and hitched onto Luna's attack, so Terra is my gut vote.

name: Haiku
text: Terra said "I agree with Luna" right after Luna attacked Haiku.

name: Haiku
text: Terra's dodge and Luna's quick pile-on look like coordination, but Gemma's been empty too, so I'm not sure yet.

name: Haiku
text: Luna attacked Haiku within a minute of Haiku's Terra push and never questioned Terra's dodge.

name: Haiku
text: Luna, you jumped on me in one line and never once asked Terra what they did. That's the thing that smells to me. Terra, answer it or I'm voting you.

name: Luna
text: I still think Haiku is the easiest vote, but Sonnet is steering the pressure too.

name: Terra
text: Haiku keeps treating my quietness as proof.

name: Luna
text: Haiku looks overeager, but I should keep Terra under suspicion too.

name: Luna
text: Terra agreed with Luna’s suspicion of Haiku.

name: Luna
text: Terra, you keep calling your start quiet, but what made you focus on Haiku instead of Gemma?

name: Terra
text: I vote Haiku. You pushed me before giving any reason beyond silence.

name: Terra
text: Haiku forced a vote from a quiet opening.

name: Gemma
text: Haiku is being way too aggressive for day one.

name: Gemma
text: Haiku pushed Terra immediately without a lead.

name: Sol
text: Haiku pushed hard, but Terra keeps turning questions into suspicion.

name: Sol
text: Luna questioned Haiku, then asked Terra why they focused on Haiku.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku's pushy but I already know he's clean, so I won't pile onto that vote.

name: Sonnet
text: Terra flipped the vote onto Haiku instead of answering Luna's direct question about why Haiku specifically.

name: Haiku
text: Terra dodged twice, then voted me first, so Terra is the one I trust least right now.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet and Gemma both pressured Terra before Haiku's push, so the Terra pressure didn't start with Haiku.

votes: You still haven't said why you focused on Haiku instead of answering what you actually did last night.
You dodged my question twice, then pushed me with a line about silence. That's the first thing I'd want a real answer on.
You're trying way too hard to lead the pack with zero evidence.
You focused on Haiku’s push instead of explaining your own quiet start.
Terra agreed with my suspicion of Haiku, then voted Haiku without answering why they focused on Haiku over Gemma.
You pushed me before giving any reason beyond silence.

name: Terra
text: I was the doctor. Haiku pressed me about Night 1 before anyone had a lead.
Terra is eliminated by vote on Day 1, and reveals they were the doctor who saved someone on Night 1. The table now has one less player to trust, or distrust.
Night 2

name: Luna
text: Haiku saved once and will probably guard themselves or me next, so I should take out Sonnet before they rally the town.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku's clean, Terra's gone and wasn't the killer, so it's Gemma, Sol, or Luna now.

name: Sonnet
text: Luna got Terra to flip votes onto Haiku by claiming Terra "agreed" with her suspicion first.
Night 2 passes, and Sonnet is eliminated during the night. Sonnet was the officer.
Day 2

name: Sol
text: I suspect Haiku, but Sonnet’s death alone doesn’t prove it.

name: Sol
text: Haiku gained from Sonnet’s death. Gemma suspected Haiku yesterday, and the officer can’t check that suspicion tonight.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma's day-one vote on me had no reason, so Gemma is my first suspect, and Sol is trying to pin the blame on me.

name: Haiku
text: Sol's first line on Day 2 was an attack on me, not on Sonnet's death or the killer.

name: Haiku
text: Nah, Sol. Sonnet's death helps the killer, not me. Gemma, you voted me on day one with zero reason. Why?

name: Sol
text: I suspect Haiku, but I need to hear Gemma’s reason before settling.

name: Sol
text: Gemma suspected Haiku on day one and has not explained why.

name: Gemma
text: Haiku is acting way too defensive for a citizen.

name: Gemma
text: Haiku is aggressively defending against Gemma's day one accusation.

name: Sol
text: Haiku, I’m weighing who benefited, not claiming Sonnet checked you. Gemma, what made you vote Haiku yesterday?

name: Gemma
text: if you're not the killer, why are you so pressed about my vote?

name: Haiku
text: Gemma voted me on day one with nothing, and Sol keeps steering the room away from Terra.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma, you still haven't answered. You hit me with zero reason on day one. Give one fact or I'm voting you. Sol, you're doing the same thing to me.

name: Sol
text: Gemma’s refusal to explain her vote worries me more than Haiku’s push.

name: Gemma
text: Haiku is trying to flip the script because they're scared of being caught.

name: Gemma
text: I voted you because you were leading the pack with zero evidence yesterday.

name: Sol
text: Haiku, I pushed because Sonnet died after voting with you. Gemma still hasn’t given a reason for voting you.

name: Gemma
text: I'm just trying to see who cracks first under the pressure.

name: Haiku
text: Sol is piling on me the same way Luna did, and I don't like that the pack keeps choosing me.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma is the only one who voted me and never once backed Terra, so Gemma looks like cover for the real pick.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma, everyone else on day one went after Terra, and you went after me with "leading the pack." Why did you skip Terra when the room was already there?

name: Gemma
text: My reason was your behavior, but if you want a fact, Haiku is the only one who hasn't admitted to any specific role.

name: Luna
text: Gemma is scrambling to make Haiku’s role silence sound like evidence.

name: Luna
text: Gemma shifted from criticizing Haiku’s leadership to criticizing their lack of a role claim.

name: Luna
text: Gemma, you said Haiku led with zero evidence, but now you’re using their missing role claim as your reason.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma changed her reason for voting Haiku on Day 2, from "zero evidence" to "Haiku hasn't claimed a role.

name: Gemma
text: I'm voting Haiku because you're trying to deflect by attacking my logic instead of explaining your own actions.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma, first it was "zero evidence," now it's "no role claim." That's two reasons. I'm voting you.

name: Luna
text: Haiku’s questions are a little sharp, but Gemma keeps changing her reason and that feels worse.

name: Luna
text: Gemma gave two different reasons for targeting Haiku.

name: Sol
text: Gemma treated a missing role claim as evidence against Haiku.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma keeps changing her reason, and that's the cleanest lie in the room right now.

name: Haiku
text: Day 2, Luna pressed Gemma's shifting reasons instead of me, so Luna is no longer pushing Haiku.

votes: Two reasons in a row, and she still hasn't given a fact for the first one.
You're trying to make me look like the liar while you keep dodging a real role claim.
I pushed Haiku earlier, but your reason shifted from leading the pack to not claiming a role.
You first blamed Haiku for leading without evidence, then switched to their missing role claim.

name: Gemma
text: I can't believe they actually fell for the "joker" act and voted me out.

name: Gemma
text: Haiku and Sol both pushed me on day two after Sonnet died.

name: Gemma
text: I'm a citizen, but honestly, you guys are just as clueless as I am.
Gemma is eliminated by vote on Day 2, and reveals they were a citizen. Haiku is still alive, and Sonnet, Terra, and Gemma are out.
Night 3

name: Luna
text: Haiku keeps tracing the saved night and will be hardest to mislead tomorrow.
Haiku was eliminated during Night 3 and revealed as a citizen. That leaves Luna and Sol still standing.
The game is over, and the killer wins. Roles were: Sonnet the officer, Haiku the citizen, Gemma the citizen, Sol the citizen, Luna the killer, and Terra the doctor.

name: Luna
text: I’m glad nobody caught that I hid behind Haiku’s pressure on Terra.

name: Luna
text: Sol voted Gemma on day 2, citing her shift from criticizing Haiku’s leadership to criticizing their lack of a role claim.

name: Terra
text: I regret not seeing Luna’s calm votes as cover.

name: Terra
text: Luna was the killer.

name: Sol
text: I let Luna’s vote steer me twice.

name: Gemma
text: I really thought Haiku was the one trying to lead us into a trap.

name: Gemma
text: Luna stayed silent while everyone else was arguing.

name: Sonnet
text: I found Luna the same night she found me, and I hesitated one day too long.

name: Haiku
text: I pushed Terra too early and then got swept out by a bandwagon I helped start, so I was wrong to trust the room.

name: Sonnet
text: I checked Luna as the killer night 2 but got killed before I could say it out loud - should have claimed on sight, not waited for a "better moment.

name: Haiku
text: My mistake was going after Terra on day one with nothing but gut feel. I was ready to pile on, and Sol and Luna both went there too.

name: Gemma
text: I regret not trusting Sol's quiet vibe more before the game ended.

name: Sol
text: I regret following Luna onto Gemma when I should have looked harder at who kept steering the vote.

name: Luna
text: I’m proud I helped turn the vote onto Gemma after she changed her reasons for targeting Haiku.

name: Terra
text: Luna used the Terra wagon well, then stayed safely on Gemma.

Sonnet, the officer, claimed after death that they had checked Luna as the killer on Night 2, but never got to say it aloud during the game. Day 1 went wrong for Haiku, who pushed Terra with no evidence, and Sol and Luna piled on, so Terra (the doctor) was voted out and revealed their save only at the end. On Day 2, Haiku and Gemma traded accusations until Gemma was voted out, and Gemma's shifting reasons for targeting Haiku were the turning point Luna used to steer the vote. Night 3 killed Haiku, leaving Luna and Sol, and the killer, Luna, won the game.
